newsitem.title: USA: "Ghost and Darkness" debuts at top of box office.
newsitem.headline: "Ghost and Darkness" debuts at top of box office.

text.p: "The Ghost and the Darkness," Paramount Pictures' adventure thriller set in Africa, squeaked past the comedy "The First Wives Club" to be the number one grossing film over the weekend.
"Ghost and Darkness," starring Val Kilmer and Michael Douglas, brought in an estimated $9.3 million in weekend ticket receipts, according to industry estimates released on Sunday.
"First Wives," also a Paramount production, came in a close second with $9.2 million.
At number three with an even $9 million was "The Long Kiss Goodnight," New Line Cinema's thriller that stars Geena Davis and was produced by her husband, Renny Harlin.
Universal's adaptation of the John Grisham novel "The Chamber" debuted at a distant fourth, bringing in $6 million in sales over the weekend.
"That Thing You Do," the Tom Hanks comedy about a struggling rock band, dropped to number five with $5.2 million in sales, after debuting in third place last week.
Box office results were complied by Los Angeles-based Exhibitor Relations.

Rounding out the top ten were "D3 The Mighty Ducks," Buena Vista's second sequal to the popular childrens' film, with $4.1 million in weekend sales; Warner Bros' "The Glimmer Man" with $4 million; Sony/Columbia's "Extreme Measures" with $1.65 million; and "Fly Away Home," a Sony production that grossed $1.6 million.
In 10th place with weekend receipts of $1.35 million was "Independence Day," the Twentieth Century Fox summertime blockbuster that is still drawing sizeable crowds 15 weeks after its release.
